investigator.method: Bounded, single unauthenticated Level-1 PASSIVE_STATIC GET (curl, descriptive User-Agent, redirects followed, 20s timeout, no retry, no authentication, no CAPTCHA/challenge bypass, no browser) against the venue's official_website (falling back to official_programme_url where noted), as part of BEATMAPPED-LONDON-SECOND-LIVE-TRANCHE-01 batch 6 of 7.

probe_history.reason: A single unauthenticated Level-1 static GET against https://eea.org.uk/events retained enough real evidence (event/programme listing content, title/meta tags, and structured data where present) to reach an honest, evidenced REJECT decision without needing to escalate to Level 2/3/4.

venue_reference: Emergency Exit Arts — Azof Street, SE10 0EF, London

identity.notes: The retained page's own <title> ('Events | EEA') and meta description ('Emergency Exit Arts (EEA) creates unforgettable events...') directly self-identify the domain as EEA's official events page.

site_classification.platform: Server-rendered static HTML event cards; retained JSON-LD on this page is limited to WebPage/LocalBusiness/BreadcrumbList schema.org types, not Event schema.

venue_location.notes: Discovery evidence reports Azof Street, SE10 0EF, London; the retained excerpt did not itself restate a street address for this bounded probe.

reasons: The retained Upcoming-events excerpt shows only two current listings: 'Quingo Starlequinn @Freedom Fesival 2026' (an outdoor drummer/visual performance hosted at a third-party festival, not at this venue's own premises) and 'Greenwich YouthFest' (an outdoor youth-club programme) — neither is a bands/concerts/DJ/classical music programme at the venue itself.

EEA's own retained meta description self-identifies the organisation as creating 'events and participatory experiences using visual performance, processions, puppetry, music and pyrotechnics' — a community/outdoor street-arts organisation for which music is one ingredient among several, not a substantially music-led venue programme.

evidence.description: Retained, bounded, genuine excerpts (contiguous literal substrings) of the actual HTTP response body from a single unauthenticated GET, plus response metadata (status/content-type/title); JSON wrapper around literal excerpt strings, so not byte-faithful as a whole file.
evidence.method: curl -L (redirects followed); descriptive User-Agent; unauthenticated GET; 20-second timeout; no retry; no browser/JS execution.
